title: Eleven Thousand Vehicles a Day
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：traffic　|　正文 360 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 traffic 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: There was no ① traffic in the village until 1961, when they put in the bypass and all the ② heavy traffic from the coast road came through for eleven years: eleven thousand vehicles a day, past eleven houses. My grandmother said the ③ traffic did not slow down at the shop and did not stop at the door, and that a road is a river with rules.

In 1972 a ④ traffic jam on the bypass lasted eleven hours, and eleven people walked into the shop and bought things they did not want, and it was the best day she ever had, and the traffic never stopped at the door. In 1974 they put ⑤ traffic lights at the top of the street, and she said the lights were not for the cars but for the children, and that everybody knew it and nobody said it.

The ⑥ traffic she never spoke about, and which I did not learn about until 1998, was in cigarettes: her brother was one of the men who ⑦ traffic in other people's weaknesses, and he did it from 1946 to 1957, eleven years, and was caught in 1957 and never went to prison, and she kept the shop open for him while he was away. My mother found the letters in 2011.

In 1989 she was ⑧ caught in traffic for the first and last time, on the way back from the hospital, eleven minutes from her own door, and she said it was the most rest she had had in thirty-one years and that nobody was to tell my grandfather. The ⑨ traffic on the bypass stopped entirely in 1998, when they opened the second road, and the village went quiet inside a week.

The ⑩ traffic, eleven thousand vehicles a day, is gone now, and there is no traffic at all and the shop is a house, and the lights at the top of the street were taken out in 2011. She died in 2003. She had said once that a road is a river with rules, and that the river remembers the village long after the village has forgotten the river, which I have never understood and have never forgotten.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 交通；通行；往来
D. v. 贩卖；非法交易（traffic in ...）
E. 固定搭配：traffic jam 交通堵塞；堵车
F. 固定搭配：heavy traffic 交通繁忙；车流量大
G. 固定搭配：traffic lights 交通信号灯；红绿灯
H. 固定搭配：be caught in traffic 遇上堵车；被困在车流中

items.q: There was no traffic in the village
all the heavy traffic from the coast road
My grandmother said the traffic did not slow
a traffic jam on the bypass lasted eleven hours
they put traffic lights at the top
The traffic she never spoke about
the men who traffic in other people's weaknesses
she was caught in traffic for the first
The traffic on the bypass stopped entirely
The traffic, eleven thousand vehicles a day

answers.why: traffic 意为“交通、往来”，1961 年以前村子里根本没有车辆往来。
heavy traffic 意为“交通繁忙、车流量大”，海滨公路上的繁忙车流有十一年都从村里穿过。
the traffic 意为“车流、往来车辆”，祖母说车流经过商店时不减速，到了门口也不停。
traffic jam 意为“交通堵塞”，1972 年绕城公路上堵了十一个小时。
traffic lights 意为“交通信号灯、红绿灯”，1974 年他们在街口装了红绿灯。
the traffic in ... 意为“……的非法买卖、贩运”，她从不提起的那宗买卖是香烟。
traffic 作动词，意为“贩卖、从事非法交易”，她弟弟是靠贩卖别人的弱点谋生的人之一。
be caught in traffic 意为“遇上堵车、被困在车流中”，1989 年她第一次也是最后一次遇上堵车。
the traffic 意为“交通、通行”，1998 年第二条路开通后，绕城公路的交通彻底停了。
the traffic 意为“车流量”，一天一万一千辆的车流如今没有了。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1961 年以前村子里根本没有车辆往来，直到他们修了绕城公路。（traffic）
海滨公路上的繁忙车流有十一年都从村里穿过。（heavy traffic）
1972 年绕城公路上堵了十一个小时，那是她生意最好的一天。（traffic jam）
1974 年他们在街口装了红绿灯，她说那是为孩子装的。（traffic lights）
她从不提起的那宗非法买卖是香烟，从 1946 年做到 1957 年。（traffic）
1989 年她第一次也是最后一次遇上堵车，离自家门口十一分钟。（be caught in traffic）
answers: There was no traffic in the village until 1961, when they put in the bypass.
All the heavy traffic from the coast road came through the village for eleven years.
In 1972 a traffic jam on the bypass lasted eleven hours, and it was the best day she ever had.
In 1974 they put traffic lights at the top of the street, and she said they were for the children.
The traffic she never spoke about was in cigarettes, from 1946 to 1957.
In 1989 she was caught in traffic for the first and last time, eleven minutes from her own door.
